| `--emb-type` | `cell` | Embedding type: `cell` for mean-pooled cell embeddings, `cge` for contextual gene embeddings |
| `--pretrained-embedding` | None | Path to pretrained embeddings for out-of-distribution species (enables embedding surgery) |
| `--model-type` | `transcriptformer` | Model architecture: `transcriptformer` or `esm2ce` |
| `--clip-counts` | `30` | Maximum count value — higher values are clipped |
| `--filter-to-vocabs` | `True` | Filter genes to only those in the model's vocabulary |
| `--use-raw` | `auto` | Use `adata.raw.X` (`True`), `adata.X` (`False`), or auto-detect (`auto`/`None`) |
| `--remove-duplicate-genes` | `False` | Remove duplicate genes instead of raising an error |
| `--num-gpus` | `1` | GPU count: `1` for single, `-1` for all available, `>1` for specific count |
| `--device` | `auto` | Device: `auto`, `cpu`, `cuda`, or `mps` |
| `--disable-compile-block-mask` | `False` | Disable block mask compilation (useful for CPU or debugging) |
| `--oom-dataloader` | `False` | Use OOM-safe map-style DataLoader with DistributedSampler |
| `--n-data-workers` | `0` | Number of DataLoader workers (leave `0` for deterministic behavior) |

Sources: [\_\_init\_\_.py](/src/transcriptformer/cli/__init__.py#L152-L201)

### Configuration Override Mechanism

Not every configuration value is exposed as a dedicated CLI flag. The `--config-override` argument lets you modify any nested configuration key using dot-path notation, and it can be specified multiple times:

```bash
transcriptformer inference \
  --checkpoint-path ./checkpoints/tf_sapiens \
  --data-file ./data/my_data.h5ad \
  --config-override model.data_config.normalize_to_scale=10000 \
  --config-override model.inference_config.obs_keys.0=cell_type
```

The override logic automatically converts values to the appropriate Python type — integers, floats, booleans (`true`/`false`), and nulls (`none`/`null`) are parsed before being applied via `OmegaConf.update`. String values that don't match any conversion rule are kept as-is. This mechanism gives you full access to every field in the configuration hierarchy without requiring a separate YAML file.

Sources: [\_\_init\_\_.py](/src/transcriptformer/cli/__init__.py#L203-L210), [\_\_init\_\_.py](/src/transcriptformer/cli/__init__.py#L310-L342)

### Three-Layer Configuration Merge

When you run `transcriptformer inference`, the configuration is assembled in three sequential layers, each overriding the previous:

1. **Base YAML config** — loaded from `src/transcriptformer/cli/conf/inference_config.yaml`, providing defaults for all settings.
2. **Checkpoint config** — the `config.json` stored inside the checkpoint directory (originally saved by MLflow during training), which carries the exact model architecture and training data settings.
3. **CLI arguments** — explicit `--flag` values and `--config-override` key=value pairs, which take the highest precedence.

This layering ensures that model-specific settings (like architecture dimensions and vocabulary paths) are always correct from the checkpoint, while you only need to specify the data path and any parameters you want to change.

Sources: [inference.py](/src/transcriptformer/cli/inference.py#L34-L43), [\_\_init\_\_.py](/src/transcriptformer/cli/__init__.py#L262-L280)

### Inference Execution Flow

Once the configuration is fully resolved, the inference pipeline proceeds through these stages:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Load vocabularies<br/>& embeddings"] --> B["Instantiate model"]
    B --> C["Load weights from<br/>model_weights.pt"]
    C --> D{"pretrained_embedding<br/>specified?"}
    D -- Yes --> E["Embedding surgery"]
    D -- No --> F["Build DataLoader"]
    E --> F
    F --> G["PyTorch Lightning<br/>Trainer.predict()"]
    G --> H["Stack & combine<br/>predictions"]
    H --> I["Write output<br/>.h5ad"]
```

The model is instantiated as a PyTorch Lightning module, loaded with `torch.load` (with `weights_only=True`) and mapped to the target device. If `pretrained_embedding` is specified, the embedding surgery step replaces the gene embedding layer to support species outside the training vocabulary. The PyTorch Lightning `Trainer` handles device placement, mixed precision, and multi-GPU distribution (DDP for `num_gpus > 1`). After prediction, outputs are stacked, combined into a new AnnData object, and written to disk.

Sources: [inference.py](/src/transcriptformer/model/inference.py#L38-L102), [\_\_init\_\_.py](/src/transcriptformer/cli/__init__.py#L344-L387)

### Output Structure

The output AnnData file's content depends on the `emb_type` and `output_keys` settings:

| `emb_type` | Storage Location | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `cell` (default) | `adata.obsm["embeddings"]` | Mean-pooled cell embeddings as a NumPy array (cells × embedding_dim) |
| `cge` | `adata.uns["cge_embeddings"]`, `adata.uns["cge_cell_indices"]`, `adata.uns["cge_gene_names"]` | Contextual gene embeddings in a flattened format with cell indices and gene name metadata |

When `output_keys` includes `llh`, zero-truncated Poisson log-likelihoods are stored in `adata.uns["llh"]`. The `obs_keys` setting (defaulting to `["all"]`) controls which observation columns from the input AnnData are carried through to the output.

> [!TIP]
> When extracting contextual gene embeddings (`--emb-type cge`), the output stores a flattened representation in `uns` rather than `obsm` because each cell can have a variable number of expressed genes. Use `uns["cge_cell_indices"]` and `uns["cge_gene_names"]` to map each embedding back to its source cell and gene.

Sources: [inference.py](/src/transcriptformer/model/inference.py#L243-L296)

### Common Inference Patterns

**Basic cell embeddings** — the most common workflow for downstream tasks like clustering or classification:

```bash
transcriptformer inference \
  --checkpoint-path ./checkpoints/tf_sapiens \
  --data-file ./data/human_pbmc.h5ad \
  --output-path ./results/pbmc \
  --batch-size 16
```

**Contextual gene embeddings** — for per-gene analysis in gene space:

```bash
transcriptformer inference \
  --checkpoint-path ./checkpoints/tf_sapiens \
  --data-file ./data/human_pbmc.h5ad \
  --emb-type cge \
  --output-filename cge_embeddings.h5ad
```

**CPU-only inference** — disable GPU compilation for debugging or machines without CUDA:

```bash
transcriptformer inference \
  --checkpoint-path ./checkpoints/tf_sapiens \
  --data-file ./data/human_pbmc.h5ad \
  --device cpu \
  --disable-compile-block-mask
```

**Out-of-distribution species via embedding surgery** — adapt a model to a species not in its training vocabulary:

```bash
transcriptformer inference \
  --checkpoint-path ./checkpoints/tf_metazoa \
  --data-file ./data/rat_data.h5ad \
  --pretrained-embedding ./checkpoints/all_embeddings/rat_embedding.pt
```

Sources: [\_\_init\_\_.py](/src/transcriptformer/cli/__init__.py#L96-L119), [inference_config.yaml](/src/transcriptformer/cli/conf/inference_config.yaml#L1-L43)

## The `download` Command

Before running inference, you need model checkpoint files. The `download` command fetches and extracts compressed model artifacts from a public S3 bucket (`czi-transcriptformer.s3.amazonaws.com/weights/`), with progress bars for both download and extraction.

### Syntax and Model Options

```bash
transcriptformer download <model> [--checkpoint-dir DIR]
```

| Model Argument | Extracted Directory | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `tf-sapiens` | `./checkpoints/tf_sapiens/` | Human-only model (368M trainable params, 23,829 vocab) |
| `tf-exemplar` | `./checkpoints/tf_exemplar/` | Human + 4 model organisms (542M trainable params, 110,290 vocab) |
| `tf-metazoa` | `./checkpoints/tf_metazoa/` | All 12 species (444M trainable params, 247,388 vocab) |
| `all` | All three + embeddings | Downloads all models and the `all_embeddings` package |
| `all-embeddings` | `./checkpoints/all_embeddings/` | Protein embeddings for 24 species (for embedding surgery) |

The `--checkpoint-dir` flag (default: `./checkpoints`) controls where files are extracted. Each extracted directory contains `model_weights.pt`, `config.json`, and a `vocabs/` subdirectory with the gene and auxiliary vocabularies.

Sources: [download_artifacts.py](/src/transcriptformer/cli/download_artifacts.py#L22-L59), [\_\_init\_\_.py](/src/transcriptformer/cli/__init__.py#L224-L239)

### Download Implementation Details

The download uses `urllib.request.urlretrieve` with a custom `reporthook` callback for progress reporting, then extracts the `.tar.gz` archive with member-by-member extraction and progress tracking. HTTP 404 errors are caught specifically to provide a clear message when a model name doesn't exist at the expected S3 path.

Sources: [download_artifacts.py](/src/transcriptformer/cli/download_artifacts.py#L61-L136)

## The `download-data` Command

The `download-data` command interfaces with the **CellxGene Discover** portal to bulk-download single-cell RNA-seq datasets filtered by species. This is useful for acquiring training or evaluation data in the AnnData format that TranscriptFormer expects.

### Syntax

```bash
transcriptformer download-data --species "homo sapiens" [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--species` | (required unless `--test-only`) | Comma-separated list of species names (e.g., `"homo sapiens,mus musculus"`) |
| `--output-dir` | `./data/cellxgene` | Directory where datasets will be saved |
| `--processes` | `4` | Number of parallel download processes |
| `--max-retries` | `5` | Maximum retry attempts per dataset |
| `--no-metadata` | flag | Skip saving dataset metadata to JSON file |
| `--test-only` | flag | Only test API connectivity, don't download |

The `--test-only` flag is a quick way to verify that the CellxGene Discover API is reachable before launching a large download. When connectivity fails, the CLI suggests running with `--test-only` to diagnose the issue.

Sources: [\_\_init\_\_.py](/src/transcriptformer/cli/__init__.py#L241-L284), [download_data.py](/src/transcriptformer/cli/download_data.py#L26-L123)

## Hydra-Based Invocation (Alternative)

In addition to the `transcriptformer` CLI, inference can be run directly via the Hydra-decorated module entry point. This approach uses `--config-name` and dot-path overrides instead of `argparse` flags:

```bash
python -m transcriptformer.cli.inference \
  --config-name=inference_config.yaml \
  model.checkpoint_path=./checkpoints/tf_sapiens \
  model.inference_config.data_files.0=test/data/human_val.h5ad \
  model.inference_config.output_path=./custom_results_dir \
  model.inference_config.batch_size=8 \
  model.inference_config.device=cuda
```

> [!TIP]
> The Hydra entry point reads its config from `src/transcriptformer/cli/conf/inference_config.yaml`, while the `transcriptformer inference` CLI loads the same file via `OmegaConf.load`. Both paths converge on the same `run_inference()` function. Use the Hydra path when you need Hydra's advanced features (like multi-run sweeps); use the `transcriptformer` CLI for everyday workflows.

Sources: [inference.py](/src/transcriptformer/cli/inference.py#L25-L71)

## End-to-End Workflow

Putting it all together, the typical workflow from a fresh installation to embeddings on disk follows this sequence:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["pip install transcriptformer"] --> B["transcriptformer download tf-sapiens()"]
    B --> C["Prepare AnnData<br/>(ensembl_id in adata.var)"]
    C --> D["transcriptformer inference()<br/>--checkpoint-path ./checkpoints/tf_sapiens<br/>--data-file my_data.h5ad"]
    D --> E["Load output .h5ad<br/>with scanpy/anndata"]
    E --> F["Downstream analysis:<br/>clustering, classification, integration"]
```

After installation, you download a model checkpoint, prepare your data as an AnnData file with gene identifiers in the `ensembl_id` column of `adata.var`, run inference, and then consume the resulting embeddings with standard scanpy/anndata tools for downstream analysis.

For deeper control over configuration values, see [Configuration Reference](16-configuration-reference). For details on cell vs. contextual gene embeddings and how to interpret them, see [Cell and Contextual Gene Embeddings](14-cell-and-contextual-gene-embeddings). For scaling inference across multiple GPUs or handling large datasets that exceed memory, see [Multi-GPU and OOM-Safe Inference](15-multi-gpu-and-oom-safe-inference).


# Cell and Contextual Gene Embeddings



TranscriptFormer produces two complementary embedding types at inference time: **cell embeddings** that represent entire cells as single vectors, and **contextual gene embeddings (CGE)** that represent each gene within the context of a specific cell. Understanding when and how to use each type is critical for extracting maximum value from the model's learned representations.

## Two Embedding Modes

The `emb_type` parameter in `InferenceConfig` governs which embedding the model returns. It accepts exactly two values — `"cell"` (default) and `"cge"` — and the validation logic enforces this constraint strictly.

| Property | Cell Embeddings | Contextual Gene Embeddings (CGE) |
|---|---|---|
| **Granularity** | One vector per cell | One vector per gene per cell |
| **Aggregation** | Mean-pooled across gene positions | No aggregation; each gene position retained |
| **Attention mode** | Bidirectional (full attention) | Bidirectional (full attention) |
| **Output shape** | `(n_cells, embed_dim)` | `(n_gene_instances, embed_dim)` |
| **Primary use cases** | Cell clustering, cell-type classification | Gene regulation analysis, gene-gene interaction, cross-cell gene behavior |
| **Storage in AnnData** | `obsm["embeddings"]` | `uns["cge_embeddings"]` + metadata arrays |

Sources: [dataclasses.py](src/transcriptformer/data/dataclasses.py#L166-L206), [model.py](src/transcriptformer/model/model.py#L337-L346)

## How Cell Embeddings Are Computed

When `emb_type="cell"`, the model's forward pass executes its full transformer encoder and then applies the `mean_embeddings` function to the gene-position outputs. This function multiplies each position's embedding by a boolean pad mask (excluding padded positions from contributing to the mean), then averages across the sequence dimension. The result is a single `embed_dim`-dimensional vector per cell that summarizes the entire transcriptomic state.

The mean-pooling step is straightforward but critical: it ensures that padding tokens — which exist simply to make rectangular batch tensors — do not dilute the embedding signal. The mask marks `True` for valid gene positions and `False` for padding, and only valid positions contribute to the average.

```python
# Simplified from the actual implementation
def mean_embeddings(embeddings, mask=None, include_masked=True):
    if mask is None:
        return embeddings.mean(dim=1)
    else:
        return (embeddings * mask.unsqueeze(-1)).sum(dim=1) / mask.sum(dim=1)
```

Sources: [layers.py](src/transcriptformer/model/layers.py#L15-L21), [model.py](src/transcriptformer/model/model.py#L344-L346)

## How Contextual Gene Embeddings Are Computed

When `emb_type="cge"`, a fundamentally different extraction path activates. Instead of pooling, the model preserves the transformer output at every individual gene position. The `_create_cge_dict` method iterates over each cell in the batch and each gene position in the sequence, building a dictionary that maps gene names (e.g., `ENSG00000152601`) to their position-specific transformer output vectors. Special tokens — `[PAD]`, `[START]`, `[END]`, `[CELL]`, `[RD]`, and `"unknown"` — are explicitly excluded from this dictionary.

The critical architectural detail is that each gene's CGE vector is **not** the pretrained protein embedding for that gene. It is the **transformer's output representation** at that gene's position after all attention layers have mixed information from every other gene in the cell. This means the same gene (e.g., MALAT1) will produce a *different* CGE vector in a T cell than in a hepatocyte, because the surrounding transcriptomic context shapes the attention-weighted representation.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Input: Gene tokens + counts per cell"] --> B["Pretrained Protein Embeddings"]
    B --> C["Flex Attention Transformer Encoder"]
    C --> D{emb_type?}
    D -->|"cell"| E["mean_embeddings() → one vector per cell"]
    D -->|"cge"| F["_create_cge_dict() → one vector per gene per cell"]
    F --> G["Filter out special tokens PAD/START/END/CELL/RD"]
    G --> H["Map token indices back to gene names"]
    E --> I["Stored in adata.obsm"]
    H --> J["Stored in adata.uns as flattened arrays"]
```

Sources: [model.py](src/transcriptformer/model/model.py#L217-L249), [model.py](src/transcriptformer/model/model.py#L337-L346)

## The Embedding-Mode Attention Switch

A subtle but important mechanism distinguishes embedding extraction from training-time forward passes: the `emb_mode` flag. When the model calls `self.forward(batch, embed=True)`, it passes `emb_mode=True` into the `_score_mod_factory`, which modifies the attention score bias logic.

During training, the count-based attention bias is applied only when `q_idx > kv_idx` (causal masking — a query position can only be biased by key positions that precede it). During embedding extraction, the condition becomes `(q_idx > kv_idx) | emb_mode`, which evaluates to `True` for all position pairs when `emb_mode=True`. This means every gene position attends to every other gene position with count-based bias, producing truly bidirectional contextual representations. Without this switch, CGE vectors would carry the artifacts of causal ordering rather than the full bidirectional context of the cell.

```python
# The score modification logic
def score_mod(score, b, h, q_idx, kv_idx):
    bias = log_counts[b, kv_idx] * ((q_idx > kv_idx) | emb_mode)
    score = score + bias
    ...
```

> [!TIP]
> The bidirectional attention in embedding mode is what makes CGE vectors *contextual* rather than merely positional. If you extract raw pretrained embeddings (the `PretrainedEmbeddings` output before the transformer), you get gene representations that are identical regardless of cell type — these are *non-contextual*. Only the transformer's output, after bidirectional attention mixing, produces embeddings that reflect the cell's transcriptomic state.

Sources: [model.py](src/transcriptformer/model/model.py#L205-L215), [model.py](src/transcriptformer/model/model.py#L311-L313)

## CGE Output Storage Format

Because CGE produces a variable number of gene vectors per cell (cells express different numbers of genes), the output cannot be stored as a simple rectangular matrix in `obsm`. Instead, the inference pipeline flattens all gene embeddings across all cells into three parallel arrays stored in the AnnData object's `uns` (unstructured annotations):

| `uns` Key | Shape | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `cge_embeddings` | `(n_gene_instances, embed_dim)` | The embedding vectors, one per gene per cell |
| `cge_cell_indices` | `(n_gene_instances,)` | Integer index mapping each embedding back to its source cell |
| `cge_gene_names` | `(n_gene_instances,)` | Gene name (e.g., Ensembl ID) for each embedding |

This flattened representation is necessary for HDF5 compatibility — `obsm` requires all arrays to share the same first dimension (number of cells), which does not hold for per-gene-per-cell data. To reconstruct per-cell gene dictionaries, you group by `cge_cell_indices`.

```python
# Example: accessing CGE data from the output AnnData
adata = ad.read_h5ad("cge_emb.h5ad")

embeddings = adata.uns['cge_embeddings']       # shape: (n_gene_instances, 2048)
cell_indices = adata.uns['cge_cell_indices']   # shape: (n_gene_instances,)
gene_names = adata.uns['cge_gene_names']       # shape: (n_gene_instances,)

# Get all embeddings for cell 0
cell_0_mask = cell_indices == 0
cell_0_genes = gene_names[cell_0_mask]
cell_0_embs = embeddings[cell_0_mask]
```

Sources: [inference.py](src/transcriptformer/model/inference.py#L264-L297)

## Running Inference for Each Embedding Type

Both embedding types are accessed through the same `transcriptformer inference` CLI command, differing only in the `--emb-type` flag.

**Cell embeddings** (default):

```bash
transcriptformer inference \
  --checkpoint-path ./checkpoints/tf_sapiens/ \
  --data-file test/data/human_val.h5ad \
  --emb-type cell \
  --output-filename cell_embeddings.h5ad
```

**Contextual gene embeddings**:

```bash
transcriptformer inference \
  --checkpoint-path ./checkpoints/tf_sapiens/ \
  --data-file test/data/human_val.h5ad \
  --emb-type cge \
  --output-filename cge_embeddings.h5ad
```

The `--emb-type` flag maps directly to `InferenceConfig.emb_type`, which is validated at initialization to be either `"cell"` or `"cge"`. Any other value raises a `ValueError`.

> [!TIP]
> CGE output is significantly larger than cell output. For a dataset of 1,000 cells with an average of ~2,000 expressed genes per cell, CGE produces ~2 million embedding vectors versus 1,000 for cell embeddings. Plan storage and downstream memory accordingly — consider filtering to specific genes of interest after extraction.

Sources: [dataclasses.py](src/transcriptformer/data/dataclasses.py#L200-L206), [contextual-gene-embeddings.ipynb](notebooks/contextual-gene-embeddings.ipynb#L167-L171)

## ESM2CE Model: CGE Without the Transformer

The `ESM2CE` model variant (selected via `model_type: esm2ce` in configuration) provides a contrasting approach to CGE. It bypasses the transformer encoder entirely and returns the **raw pretrained protein embeddings** as the CGE vectors, accessed via `PretrainedEmbeddings.forward(x, embed_only=True)`. Because these embeddings have not passed through any attention layers, they are identical for a given gene regardless of which cell that gene appears in — they are *non-contextual* gene representations.

This variant serves as a useful baseline: comparing ESM2CE CGE vectors against TranscriptFormer CGE vectors for the same gene reveals exactly how much contextual information the transformer contributes. If TranscriptFormer's CGE for gene X clusters by cell type while ESM2CE's does not, that differential is purely attributable to the transformer's cross-gene attention.

Sources: [model.py](src/transcriptformer/model/model.py#L482-L526)

## Downstream Analysis Patterns

The CGE format enables analyses that are impossible with cell-level embeddings alone. Two primary patterns emerge from the notebook tutorial:

**Gene behavior across cell types** — By selecting all CGE vectors for a single gene across many cells and projecting with UMAP, you can visualize how that gene's representation shifts depending on cellular context. If the same gene clusters by cell type in CGE space, the transformer has captured cell-type-specific regulation.

**Gene identity vs. cell identity disentanglement** — A joint UMAP of CGE vectors from multiple genes, colored by gene identity on one panel and cell type on the other, reveals whether the embedding space primarily separates by gene identity or by cellular context. The notebook demonstrates this with 10 randomly sampled genes, producing side-by-side UMAP plots colored by cell type and gene name respectively.

```python
# Pattern: filter CGE to a specific gene across all cells
gene_mask = np.isin(adata.uns['cge_gene_names'], ['ENSG00000152601'])
gene_embs = adata.uns['cge_embeddings'][gene_mask]
gene_cells = adata.uns['cge_cell_indices'][gene_mask]
cell_types = adata.obs['cell_type'].iloc[gene_cells].values

# UMAP projection
reducer = umap.UMAP(n_neighbors=15, min_dist=0.5)
embedding_2d = reducer.fit_transform(gene_embs)
```

Sources: [contextual-gene-embeddings.ipynb](notebooks/contextual-gene-embeddings.ipynb#L316-L393)

## Configuring Embedding Extraction

The following `InferenceConfig` fields directly control embedding behavior:

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `emb_type` | `str` | `"cell"` | `"cell"` for mean-pooled cell embeddings, `"cge"` for contextual gene embeddings |
| `output_keys` | `list` | `["embeddings"]` | Which outputs to include; must contain `"embeddings"` for either mode |
| `output_filename` | `str` | `"embeddings.h5ad"` | Filename for the output AnnData file |
| `batch_size` | `int` | `8` | Batch size during inference; affects memory usage significantly for CGE |
| `precision` | `str` | `"16-mixed"` | Numerical precision; CGE benefits from higher precision for downstream cosine similarity |

Sources: [dataclasses.py](src/transcriptformer/data/dataclasses.py#L188-L209), [inference_config.yaml](conf/inference_config.yaml#L7-L23)

# Multi-GPU and OOM-Safe Inference



Transcriptformer's inference pipeline is built on PyTorch Lightning and provides two complementary strategies for scaling to large datasets: **multi-GPU parallelism** via Distributed Data Parallel (DDP), and **out-of-memory (OOM)-safe data loading** via memory-mapped backed reads. These mechanisms can be combined—running OOM-safe loading across multiple GPUs—to process datasets that exceed both single-device compute capacity and single-node RAM. This page explains the architecture behind both strategies, their configuration, and the operational considerations that govern their correct use.

## Device Selection and Multi-GPU Architecture

The inference runtime determines device placement through a two-tier resolution process. The `device` parameter (`auto`, `cpu`, `cuda`, `mps`) establishes the accelerator type, while `num_gpus` controls GPU count when the accelerator is `gpu`. The `auto` device preference cascades through CUDA → MPS → CPU based on availability, whereas explicit choices (`cuda`, `mps`) raise a `RuntimeError` if the requested backend is unavailable. For multi-GPU, `num_gpus` accepts three modes: `1` for single-GPU (default), any integer `>1` for a specific GPU count, or `-1` to use all visible GPUs. When requesting more GPUs than available, the system logs a warning and falls back to the detectable count.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["device preference"] --> B{"auto?"}
    B -- Yes --> C{"CUDA available?"}
    C -- Yes --> D["accelerator = gpu"]
    C -- No --> E{"MPS available?"}
    E -- Yes --> F["accelerator = mps"]
    E -- No --> G["accelerator = cpu"]
    B -- No --> H{"cpu | cuda | mps?"}
    H -- cpu --> G
    H -- cuda --> I{"CUDA available?"}
    I -- Yes --> D
    I -- No --> J["RuntimeError"]
    H -- mps --> K{"MPS available?"}
    K -- Yes --> F
    K -- No --> J

    D --> L{"num_gpus?"}
    L -- "-1" --> M["devices = all visible GPUs"]
    L -- "> 1" --> N{"requested ≤ available?"}
    N -- Yes --> O["devices = num_gpus"]
    N -- No --> P["devices = available (with warning)"]
    L -- "1" --> Q["devices = 1"]

    M --> R["Trainer(strategy=ddp)"]
    O --> R
    P --> R
    Q --> S["Trainer(strategy=auto)"]
```

Once device resolution completes, the system constructs a PyTorch Lightning `Trainer`. The critical architectural decision occurs at the strategy level: when `devices > 1`, the trainer uses `"ddp"` (Distributed Data Parallel); otherwise it defaults to `"auto"`. DDP replicates the model across GPUs, shards the dataset via `DistributedSampler`, and synchronizes gradients—though for inference (predict-only), the synchronization overhead is minimal since no backward pass occurs. Each rank processes its shard independently and produces a subset of predictions, which the `stack_dict` utility then concatenates into a unified result.

| Parameter | Values | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `device` | `auto` | Cascade: CUDA → MPS → CPU |
| `device` | `cpu` | Force CPU, single device |
| `device` | `cuda` | Force GPU, raises if unavailable |
| `device` | `mps` | Force Apple Silicon MPS, raises if unavailable |
| `num_gpus` | `1` (default) | Single GPU, `strategy="auto"` |
| `num_gpus` | `>1` | Multi-GPU, `strategy="ddp"` |
| `num_gpus` | `-1` | All visible GPUs, `strategy="ddp"` |
| `precision` | `16-mixed` (default) | Mixed-precision inference with FP16 |

Sources: [inference.py](/src/transcriptformer/model/inference.py#L170-L247), [dataclasses.py](/src/transcriptformer/data/dataclasses.py#L166-L209)

## OOM-Safe Data Loading with AnnDatasetOOM

The standard `AnnDataset` loads entire AnnData files into memory, densifies sparse count matrices, and tokenizes all cells upfront during initialization. This is efficient for moderate datasets but becomes a memory bottleneck when processing atlases with millions of cells or tens of thousands of genes—the dense count matrix alone for a 1M × 30K dataset exceeds 100 GB in FP32. The `AnnDatasetOOM` class solves this by adopting a fundamentally different data access pattern.

`AnnDatasetOOM` opens each H5AD file in **backed mode** (`backed="r"`), which uses HDF5 memory-mapped access to read data on-demand without loading the full matrix into RAM. During initialization, it scans only the metadata—gene names, filtering indices, and row counts—to build a cumulative offset table (`_offsets`). This offset table enables O(1) global-to-file-and-row index resolution via `np.searchsorted`, making the dataset a proper map-style `Dataset` compatible with PyTorch's `DistributedSampler`.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Init as __init__
    participant H5AD as backed H5AD file
    participant GetItem as __getitem__
    participant Process as process_batch

    Init->>H5AD: anndata.read_h5ad(path, backed="r")
    H5AD-->>Init: memory-mapped handle
    Init->>H5AD: load gene names + filter indices
    Init->>Init: build _offsets = cumsum([0, n_obs...])

    loop For each inference request
        GetItem->>GetItem: _loc(idx) → (file_id, row)
        GetItem->>H5AD: X[row] (on-demand read)
        H5AD-->>GetItem: sparse row slice
        GetItem->>GetItem: densify single row
        GetItem->>Process: process_batch(1-row)
        Process-->>GetItem: BatchData token
    end
```

On each `__getitem__` call, the dataset resolves the global index to a (file, row) pair, reads only that single row from the backed matrix, densifies it (a single row is negligible in memory), and passes it through the standard `process_batch` pipeline for tokenization, padding, and normalization. This per-item processing trades throughput for memory efficiency—each worker holds only the backed file handle and a single row in memory at any time. The `collate_fn` is reused directly from `AnnDataset`, ensuring identical batch assembly semantics.

> [!TIP]
> Enable OOM-safe loading by setting `use_oom_dataloader: true` in your inference config. The standard `AnnDataset` densifies the entire count matrix during initialization, which can silently consume all available RAM on large datasets. `AnnDatasetOOM` avoids this entirely by reading one row at a time from the backed H5AD file.

The following table contrasts the two dataset implementations across key operational dimensions:

| Dimension | `AnnDataset` (in-memory) | `AnnDatasetOOM` (backed) |
|---|---|---|
| **Initialization** | Loads all files, densifies, tokenizes all cells | Opens backed handles, builds offset table only |
| **Memory footprint** | O(cells × genes) for dense matrix | O(1) per worker—only one row at a time |
| **`__getitem__` cost** | Simple tensor indexing (fast) | Disk read + densify + tokenize (slower) |
| **Sampler compatibility** | Any PyTorch sampler | `DistributedSampler` (map-style with `__len__`) |
| **DDP sharding** | Manual or via sampler | Automatic via `DistributedSampler` |
| **Activation** | Default (`use_oom_dataloader: false`) | `use_oom_dataloader: true` |

Sources: [dataloader.py](/src/transcriptformer/data/dataloader.py#L286-L653), [inference.py](/src/transcriptformer/model/inference.py#L139-L158), [dataclasses.py](/src/transcriptformer/data/dataclasses.py#L198-L198)

## Combining Multi-GPU and OOM-Safe Inference

The two strategies compose naturally: when `use_oom_dataloader` is `true` and `num_gpus > 1`, the Lightning Trainer instantiates DDP, which wraps the DataLoader with a `DistributedSampler`. Because `AnnDatasetOOM` is a map-style dataset with a well-defined `__len__`, the sampler automatically shards cell indices across GPU ranks—each rank processes a disjoint subset of rows, reads only its shard from disk, and produces predictions for its partition. The final `stack_dict` call in `run_inference` concatenates all rank outputs into the complete result.

The complete configuration for combined multi-GPU + OOM-safe inference looks like this:

```yaml
model:
  inference_config:
    use_oom_dataloader: true
    num_gpus: -1          # Use all visible GPUs
    device: cuda
    batch_size: 4         # Per-GPU batch size; total = batch_size × num_gpus
    precision: 16-mixed   # Reduce memory via mixed-precision
```

Note that `batch_size` is per-process: each GPU rank creates its own DataLoader with the configured batch size, so the effective global batch size is `batch_size × num_gpus`. For memory-constrained scenarios, reducing the per-GPU batch size is the primary lever.

> [!TIP]
> Flex Attention requires the batch size to be compatible with the block length (`model_config.block_len`, default 128). The model's `inference()` method validates this constraint at runtime. If you encounter shape mismatches with multi-GPU DDP, ensure your per-GPU batch size is a multiple of `block_len`—or use a small enough batch size that the padding logic handles it.

Sources: [inference.py](/src/transcriptformer/model/inference.py#L139-L168), [inference.py](/src/transcriptformer/model/inference.py#L239-L254), [model.py](/src/transcriptformer/model/model.py#L385-L399), [inference_config.yaml](/conf/inference_config.yaml#L1-L36)

## Checkpoint Loading and Device Mapping

Checkpoint loading is device-aware: the `map_location` for `torch.load` is resolved using the same device preference logic before the Trainer initializes. This ensures that model weights are placed on the correct device from the start, avoiding unnecessary CPU→GPU transfers. The system loads weights with `weights_only=True` for security, then applies `model.load_state_dict()` directly. If embedding surgery is configured (`pretrained_embedding` is not null), it is performed after weight loading but before the Trainer takes ownership of the model—ensuring the surgical modifications are present on all DDP replicas.

Sources: [inference.py](/src/transcriptformer/model/inference.py#L86-L118)

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Likely Cause | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| `RuntimeError: CUDA requested but not available` | `device: cuda` with no GPU | Set `device: auto` or `device: cpu` |
| OOM kill during initialization | `AnnDataset` densifying large matrix | Set `use_oom_dataloader: true` |
| Slow iteration with OOM loader | Per-item disk reads + tokenization | Increase `n_data_workers`; ensure SSD storage |
| Uneven DDP predictions | `drop_last=False` (default) + non-divisible dataset | Expected behavior; empty batches are handled by `stack_dict` |
| Flex Attention batch shape error | Per-GPU batch size incompatible with `block_len` | Set `batch_size` to a multiple of `block_len` (default 128) |
| Warning: fewer GPUs than requested | `num_gpus` exceeds `torch.cuda.device_count()` | Reduce `num_gpus` or use `-1` for auto-detection |

Sources: [inference.py](/src/transcriptformer/model/inference.py#L180-L198), [inference.py](/src/transcriptformer/model/inference.py#L239-L247)

- For single-GPU inference usage and CLI commands, see [CLI Inference Commands](13-cli-inference-commands).

# Configuration Reference



Transcriptformer uses **Hydra** with OmegaConf to manage its configuration hierarchy, enabling YAML-based defaults with full command-line override support. Understanding the configuration system is essential for controlling inference behavior, data preprocessing, device placement, and output format — all without modifying source code. This reference covers every user-facing parameter, its type, default value, and effect on the pipeline.

## Configuration Architecture

The configuration is split across two sources that merge at runtime: the **YAML file** (`inference_config.yaml`) provides user-tunable defaults, while the **checkpoint's `config.json`** supplies the frozen model architecture parameters (`model_config`, `loss_config`, and training-time `data_config` fields). The CLI entry point loads both, with the YAML file taking precedence on overlapping keys — meaning you can always override a checkpoint-derived value from the command line.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["inference_config.yaml<br/>(Hydra YAML)"] --> C{OmegaConf.merge}
    B["config.json<br/>(from checkpoint)"] --> C
    C --> D["Unified Config<br/>(cfg.model.*)"]
    D --> E["model.inference_config"]
    D --> F["model.data_config"]
    D --> G["model.model_config"]
    D --> H["model.loss_config"]
    E --> I["run_inference()"]
    F --> I
    G --> I
    H --> I
    style A fill:#2d5a8a,color:#fff
    style B fill:#5a2d8a,color:#fff
    style C fill:#1a7a4a,color:#fff
```

The YAML file defines three user-facing groups — `model.checkpoint_path`, `model.inference_config`, and `model.data_config` — while `model.model_config` and `model.loss_config` are populated exclusively from the checkpoint's stored training configuration. The inference script also auto-resolves three paths from `checkpoint_path`: `load_checkpoint` (model weights), `aux_vocab_path`, and `esm2_mappings_path`.

Sources: [inference.py](/src/transcriptformer/cli/inference.py#L33-L53), [inference_config.yaml](/src/transcriptformer/cli/conf/inference_config.yaml#L1-L43)

## Top-Level Model Section

The `model` key is the root namespace for all configuration. Only two fields are set directly at this level:

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `checkpoint_path` | `str \| null` | `null` | **Required.** Path to the model checkpoint directory (e.g., `./checkpoints/tf_sapiens`). Must contain `model_weights.pt`, `config.json`, and a `vocabs/` subdirectory. |
| `model_type` | `str` | `"transcriptformer"` | Model class to instantiate. `"transcriptformer"` for the full model, `"esm2ce"` for the ESM2 cross-encoder variant. |

The `checkpoint_path` is the single most important parameter — the inference script resolves all derivative paths from it. Setting it is mandatory; omitting it will cause a failure when the script attempts to read `config.json` or load weights.

Sources: [inference.py](/src/transcriptformer/cli/inference.py#L41-L53), [inference_config.yaml](/src/transcriptformer/cli/conf/inference_config.yaml#L4-L6)

## Inference Config (`model.inference_config`)

The `inference_config` group controls **how inference runs**: batching, device placement, output format, and embedding extraction mode. It maps to the `InferenceConfig` dataclass and is the most commonly overridden section.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Valid Values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `batch_size` | `int` | `8` | Positive integer | Number of cells processed per forward pass. Increase for throughput on large GPUs; decrease to reduce peak memory. |
| `output_keys` | `list[str]` | `["embeddings"]` | `"embeddings"`, `"llh"` | Which outputs to include in the result AnnData. `"embeddings"` stores cell or gene embeddings in `obsm`; `"llh"` stores zero-truncated Poisson log-likelihoods in `uns`. |
| `obs_keys` | `list[str]` | `["all"]` | `"all"` or column names | Which `obs` columns to pass through to the output. `"all"` copies every column; specify individual names (e.g., `"cell_type"`, `"tissue"`) for a leaner output. |
| `data_files` | `list[str]` | `["test/data/human_val.h5ad"]` | Paths to `.h5ad` files | Input AnnData files. Accepts one or more paths; all are concatenated during loading. |
| `output_path` | `str` | `"./inference_results"` | Any directory path | Directory where the output `.h5ad` file is written. Created automatically if it does not exist. |
| `output_filename` | `str` | `"embeddings.h5ad"` | Any filename | Name of the output file within `output_path`. |
| `load_checkpoint` | `str \| null` | `null` | Path to `.pt` file | **Auto-resolved.** Set internally to `{checkpoint_path}/model_weights.pt`. Do not set manually unless you have a non-standard layout. |
| `pretrained_embedding` | `str \| list \| null` | `null` | Path(s) to embedding files | Path to pretrained protein embeddings for out-of-distribution species. Triggers [Embedding Surgery](10-embedding-surgery-for-new-species). Accepts a single path or list. |
| `precision` | `str` | `"16-mixed"` | `"16-mixed"`, `"32"`, `"bf16-mixed"` | PyTorch Lightning numerical precision. `"16-mixed"` uses FP16 with mixed-precision autocasting for speed; `"32"` uses full float32 for maximum numerical fidelity. |
| `emb_type` | `str` | `"cell"` | `"cell"`, `"cge"` | Embedding extraction mode. `"cell"` returns mean-pooled cell embeddings in `obsm["embeddings"]`; `"cge"` returns per-gene contextual embeddings in `uns["cge_embeddings"]` with associated metadata. |
| `num_gpus` | `int` | `1` | `-1`, `1`, or positive int | Number of GPUs. `1` = single GPU, `-1` = all available GPUs, `N>1` = use N GPUs (falls back if fewer available). Multi-GPU uses DDP strategy. |
| `device` | `str` | `"auto"` | `"auto"`, `"cpu"`, `"cuda"`, `"mps"` | Device selection. `"auto"` picks CUDA → MPS → CPU in priority order. `"mps"` targets Apple Silicon. |
| `use_oom_dataloader` | `bool` | `false` | `true`, `false` | Switch to the OOM-safe `AnnDatasetOOM` that uses memory-mapped backed reads and per-item processing instead of loading everything into RAM. See [Multi-GPU and OOM-Safe Inference](15-multi-gpu-and-oom-safe-inference). |
| `num_nodes` | `int` | `1` | Positive integer | Number of compute nodes for distributed inference (advanced). |
| `special_tokens` | `list[str]` | `[]` | Any token strings | Additional special tokens to register during inference. |

> [!TIP]
> When extracting contextual gene embeddings (`emb_type: "cge"`), output is stored in `uns` rather than `obsm` because each cell produces a variable-length set of gene embeddings. The `uns` dict contains three parallel arrays — `cge_embeddings`, `cge_cell_indices`, and `cge_gene_names` — that you must join to reconstruct per-cell gene embedding tables.

The `output_keys` and `emb_type` parameters interact: setting `output_keys: ["embeddings"]` with `emb_type: "cge"` changes where embeddings are stored (from `obsm` to `uns`) and their shape (from cell-level vectors to per-gene vectors). Setting `output_keys: ["llh"]` adds zero-truncated Poisson log-likelihoods, useful for evaluating model fit on held-out data.

Sources: [dataclasses.py](/src/transcriptformer/data/dataclasses.py#L167-L209), [inference_config.yaml](/src/transcriptformer/cli/conf/inference_config.yaml#L8-L29), [inference.py](/src/transcriptformer/model/inference.py#L258-L310)

## Data Config (`model.data_config`)

The `data_config` group controls **how input AnnData is preprocessed** before entering the model. These parameters govern gene filtering, count normalization, and tokenization behavior — all of which must match the assumptions the model was trained under.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gene_col_name` | `str` | `"ensembl_id"` | Column in `adata.var` containing gene identifiers. Must contain Ensembl-style IDs (version suffixes are auto-stripped). |
| `clip_counts` | `float` | `30` | Maximum count value. Counts exceeding this are clamped. Matches the model's training-time clipping — do not change unless you know the checkpoint was trained with a different value. |
| `filter_to_vocabs` | `bool` | `true` | Whether to remove genes not present in the model's vocabulary. When `true`, out-of-vocabulary genes are silently dropped. When `false`, they will cause tokenization errors. |
| `filter_outliers` | `float` | `0.0` | Standard-deviation threshold for filtering outlier cells by total expression. `0.0` disables filtering. A value of `3.0` removes cells whose total counts fall outside ±3σ from the mean. |
| `normalize_to_scale` | `float` | `0` | Library-size normalization target. `0` disables normalization. A value of `10000` would normalize each cell's counts to sum to 10,000. Most checkpoints expect raw (unnormalized) counts. |
| `sort_genes` | `bool` | `false` | Whether to sort genes by descending expression level per cell. Used for ablation studies; default ordering preserves original AnnData column order for expressed genes. |
| `randomize_genes` | `bool` | `false` | Whether to randomize gene order within each cell. Also used for ablation; enabling this introduces stochasticity into the embeddings. |
| `min_expressed_genes` | `int` | `0` | Minimum number of expressed (non-zero) genes required per cell. Cells below this threshold are filtered out. Useful for excluding low-quality cells. |
| `use_raw` | `str \| bool \| null` | `"auto"` | Which count matrix to use: `true` forces `adata.raw.X`, `false` forces `adata.X`, `"auto"` (or `null`) tries `raw.X` first and falls back to `X`. |
| `remove_duplicate_genes` | `bool` | `false` | Whether to silently remove duplicate gene IDs (after version stripping) instead of raising an error. Keeps the first occurrence. |
| `n_data_workers` | `int` | `0` | Number of DataLoader workers. `0` means data loading happens in the main process, ensuring deterministic behavior. Increase for faster I/O on SSD-backed storage. |

> [!TIP]
> The `use_raw: "auto"` setting implements a sensible fallback: if the AnnData object has a `raw` slot (common in Scanpy workflows where `raw` stores pre-normalized counts), Transcriptformer will prefer it. If your data only has `X`, this works transparently. If you have both and want the processed `X` rather than `raw.X`, explicitly set `use_raw: false`.

The data pipeline applies these parameters in a specific order: (1) load gene names and auto-strip version suffixes, (2) remove duplicate genes if `remove_duplicate_genes` is true, (3) select the count matrix layer via `use_raw`, (4) filter to vocabulary genes if `filter_to_vocabs` is true, (5) filter outlier cells by expression if `filter_outliers > 0`, (6) filter cells by minimum expressed genes, (7) sort or randomize gene order, (8) normalize and clip counts. This ordering matters because, for example, `filter_outliers` operates on counts before normalization.

Sources: [dataclasses.py](/src/transcriptformer/data/dataclasses.py#L93-L150), [inference_config.yaml](/src/transcriptformer/cli/conf/inference_config.yaml#L30-L43), [dataloader.py](/src/transcriptformer/data/dataloader.py#L39-L80), [dataloader.py](/src/transcriptformer/data/dataloader.py#L230-L276)

## Checkpoint-Derived Config (`model.model_config` and `model.loss_config`)

When the inference script loads a checkpoint, it reads `config.json` from the checkpoint directory and merges it into the configuration. This file contains the **frozen training-time parameters** that define the model architecture and loss function. These are not exposed in the YAML file because changing them would break weight compatibility.

### Model Architecture Parameters (`model.model_config`)

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `num_heads` | `int` | `16` | Number of attention heads in the transformer encoder. |
| `num_layers` | `int` | `12` | Number of transformer layers. |
| `model_dim` | `int` | `2048` | Hidden dimension of the transformer. |
| `embed_dim` | `int` | `2048` | Dimension of protein embeddings (must match ESM2 output). |
| `dropout` | `float` | `0.1` | Dropout rate applied in attention and feed-forward layers. |
| `activation` | `str` | `"gelu"` | Activation function in feed-forward layers. |
| `seq_len` | `int` | `2047` | Maximum gene sequence length (number of gene tokens per cell). |
| `aux_len` | `int` | `1` | Number of auxiliary token slots. `seq_len + aux_len` must be divisible by `block_len`. |
| `block_len` | `int` | `128` | Block length for FlexAttention block masking. |
| `mu_link_fn` | `str` | `"softmax"` | Link function for the count decoder's rate parameter. Must be one of: `exp`, `log`, `relu`, `sigmoid`, `softplus`, `linear`, `softmax`. |
| `softcap` | `int` | `10` | Logit soft-cap value for the gene ID prediction head. |
| `attn_bias` | `bool` | `false` | Whether attention layers use bias terms. |
| `fw_bias` | `bool` | `false` | Whether feed-forward layers use bias terms. |
| `gene_head_hidden_dim` | `int` | `2048` | Hidden dimension of the gene ID prediction MLP head. |
| `use_aux` | `bool` | `false` | Whether auxiliary (metadata) tokens are included in the sequence. |
| `compile_block_mask` | `bool` | `true` | Whether to compile the FlexAttention block mask for performance. |

### Loss Parameters (`model.loss_config`)

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gene_id_loss_weight` | `float` | `1.0` | Weight of the gene ID prediction cross-entropy loss. Set to `0` to disable the gene ID head entirely. |
| `softplus_approx` | `bool` | `true` | Whether to use the approximate softplus in the zero-truncated Poisson loss for numerical stability. |

These checkpoint-derived parameters are validated on load — for instance, `seq_len + aux_len` must be divisible by `block_len`, and `mu_link_fn` must be one of the enumerated link functions. Changing these values without retraining would produce garbage output.

Sources: [dataclasses.py](/src/transcriptformer/data/dataclasses.py#L14-L73), [dataclasses.py](/src/transcriptformer/data/dataclasses.py#L153-L163), [inference.py](/src/transcriptformer/cli/inference.py#L41-L47)

## Hydra Override Syntax

Transcriptformer uses Hydra's override syntax to modify any configuration value from the command line without editing the YAML file. The dot-notation maps directly to the nested config structure:

```bash
python inference.py \
  --config-name=inference_config.yaml \
  model.checkpoint_path=./checkpoints/tf_sapiens \
  model.inference_config.data_files.0=my_data.h5ad \
  model.inference_config.batch_size=16 \
  model.inference_config.device=cuda \
  model.inference_config.precision=32 \
  model.data_config.clip_counts=30 \
  model.data_config.use_raw=false
```

**List overrides** use indexed syntax: `model.inference_config.data_files.0=path1.h5ad`, `model.inference_config.data_files.1=path2.h5ad`. To append without indexing, use the `+` prefix: `+model.inference_config.output_keys.0=llh`.

**Null handling**: The `checkpoint_path` defaults to `null` in the YAML. You must supply it via command line — the script will fail immediately if it is not set, since it needs to read `config.json` from that directory.

The `--config-name` flag can also point to a custom YAML file if you maintain multiple configuration profiles (e.g., one per model variant or experiment). Hydra searches the `conf/` directory relative to the script location.

Sources: [inference.py](/src/transcriptformer/cli/inference.py#L1-L18), [inference.py](/src/transcriptformer/cli/inference.py#L33-L53), [inference_config.yaml](/src/transcriptformer/cli/conf/inference_config.yaml#L1-L6)

## Configuration Quick Reference by Use Case

| Use Case | Key Overrides |
|---|---|
| **Basic inference** | `model.checkpoint_path`, `model.inference_config.data_files.0` |
| **Large datasets (OOM risk)** | `model.inference_config.use_oom_dataloader=true`, `model.inference_config.batch_size=4` |
| **Multi-GPU** | `model.inference_config.num_gpus=-1`, `model.inference_config.use_oom_dataloader=true` |
| **Apple Silicon** | `model.inference_config.device=mps` |
| **CPU-only** | `model.inference_config.device=cpu`, `model.inference_config.batch_size=1` |
| **Contextual gene embeddings** | `model.inference_config.emb_type=cge` |
| **Log-likelihood output** | `+model.inference_config.output_keys.0=llh` |
| **New species (embedding surgery)** | `model.inference_config.pretrained_embedding=path/to/emb` |
| **Filtered obs columns** | `model.inference_config.obs_keys.0=cell_type`, `model.inference_config.obs_keys.1=tissue` |
| **Full precision** | `model.inference_config.precision=32` |

Sources: [inference.py](/src/transcriptformer/cli/inference.py#L1-L18), [inference_config.yaml](/src/transcriptformer/cli/conf/inference_config.yaml#L1-L43)
